page: OVHcloud b3-8 is a General Purpose cloud server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.3 GHz. The instance provides 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with 1 thread per core. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled as a 50 GB local NVMe SSD, and the network configuration includes a baseline bandwidth of 0 Gbps alongside one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals a divergence between single-core and multi-core performance. The server demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng and Geekbench tests, placing in the top 25%. Geekbench text processing also ranks in the top 25%. However, multi-core performance in stress-ng is average, and Geekbench multi-core results fall into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth tests show average performance for large block reads and writes, but small block cached reads are weak. The server also records weak performance in Passmark CPU, memory, and database operations, as well as in Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation and balanced vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the instance offers a stable resource profile for general-purpose workloads. However, the 0 Gbps baseline network bandwidth and weak multi-threaded performance present clear tradeoffs for network-heavy or highly parallelized tasks. For LLM inference, the server handles small 135M models with average efficiency but struggles with medium 7B models. This hardware profile is best suited for lightweight single-threaded applications, basic text processing, development environments, and low-traffic web serving where dedicated CPU resources are required but network throughput is not a primary constraint.
